Connect to an xarray object

Source: R/driver.R
dbConnect-XarrayDriver-method.Rd

Exactly one of dsn, builder, object must be supplied.

Usage

# S4 method for class 'XarrayDriver'
dbConnect(
  drv,
  dsn = NULL,
  ...,
  open = "open_dataset",
  builder = NULL,
  object = NULL
)

Arguments

drv

result of xarray()

dsn

character string openable by xarray

...

keyword arguments passed to the xarray open function

open

name of the xarray open function, default "open_dataset"

builder

function taking the xarray module, returning a Dataset

object

an existing Python xarray object to adopt

Value

an XarrayConnection

Details

  • dsn: a string that xarray can open. Passed to xr.<open>(dsn, ...) where open is "open_dataset" by default (also useful: "open_zarr", which defaults to dask, so pass chunks = reticulate::py_none() for the lazy path; "open_mfdataset", which needs dask, reticulate::py_require("dask"); and "open_datatree"). Extra named arguments in ... are passed through as Python keyword arguments, e.g. engine = "h5netcdf", decode_times = TRUE, or chunks = reticulate::dict() (Python chunks={}: dask at the storage chunking; an R list() would become a Python list). engine = "gdalxarray" opens anything GDAL reads (it needs the GDAL Python bindings; see xrdbi-package). It uses GDAL's multidimensional API by default; multidim = FALSE uses the classic raster API, where a GeoTIFF or COG becomes one variable, band_data, over (band, y, x).

  • builder: an R function of one argument (the xarray module, not converted) returning a Dataset. Use this when construction needs more than a single open call, e.g. virtualizarr or icechunk session setup.

  • object: an existing reticulate Python object (an xarray Dataset), adopted as-is. Handy when the object was built interactively with reticulate::py_run_string() or in a repl.

The connection holds a reference to the Python object. Opening reads metadata; data are read when a result is fetched (see XarrayResult for statements that compute).

See also

XarrayConnection for what a connection offers; XarrayResult to query it with Python statements; tbl() to query it with dplyr verbs; the Python requirements in xrdbi-package for the engines a source needs.

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
## needs a Python environment with xarray (see ?xrdbi)
f <- system.file("extdata/autotest/trmm.nc", package = "xrdbi")
con <- dbConnect(xarray(), f)

## anything that takes more than one call
con <- dbConnect(xarray(), builder = function(xr) {
  xr$open_dataset(f)$rename(list(pcp = "precip"))
})
dbListTables(con)

## many files as one dataset (open_mfdataset needs dask)
reticulate::py_require("dask")
files <- c(f, f)  # e.g. a daily series of files on one grid
con <- dbConnect(xarray(), builder = function(xr) {
  xr$open_mfdataset(files, combine = "nested", concat_dim = "run")
})

## an object already built in the session
reticulate::py_run_string("import xarray; myds = xarray.Dataset()")
con <- dbConnect(xarray(), object = reticulate::py_eval("myds", convert = FALSE))
} # }
